articles.title: Your coding agent can read your .env. Here's how I reduced the risk
articles.excerpt: If a coding agent can read your project files, assume it can read your .env too. Ignore rules and editor settings can help, but they are not a security boundary. I moved secret values out of my projec…
articles.body: If a coding agent can read your project files, assume it can read your .env too. Ignore rules and editor settings can help, but they are not a security boundary. I moved secret values out of my project files and into 1Password, then used the CLI to provide them to the processes that need them. That reduces one easy way for an agent to discover secrets. It does not make secrets safe from code the agent writes or commands it runs. I’ll cover that part too. The idea Before, my project had a file containing actual values: # .env STRIPE_API_KEY=replace-with-your-key SENTRY_TOKEN=replace-with-your-token API_URL=http://localhost:8787 Now, the shared secrets live in 1Password.

articles.title: Laravel 13 CORS Configuration: How to Fix CORS Errors in Your API
articles.excerpt: To configure CORS in Laravel 13, publish the config file with php artisan config:publish cors, then set paths, allowed_origins, allowed_methods and allowed_headers in config/cors.php. Laravel's built-…
articles.body: To configure CORS in Laravel 13, publish the config file with php artisan config:publish cors , then set paths , allowed_origins , allowed_methods and allowed_headers in config/cors.php . Laravel's built-in CORS middleware reads that file and answers preflight OPTIONS requests for you. What is CORS and when do you need it? Browsers block JavaScript on one origin (scheme, host and port) from reading responses from another origin unless the server allows it with CORS headers. You need to configure it when a separate frontend, for example a React app on http://localhost:5173 , calls your Laravel API on http://localhost:8000 . What do you need before you start? Laravel 13 on PHP 8.3 or newer A frontend on a different origin that calls your API How do you publish the CORS config?

articles.title: 10 AI Prompts Every Developer Should Know
articles.excerpt: I think most developers are underusing AI. Not because they don't know which tools to use. Not because they haven't tried the latest coding assistants. And certainly not because they don't know how to…
articles.body: I think most developers are underusing AI. Not because they don't know which tools to use. Not because they haven't tried the latest coding assistants. And certainly not because they don't know how to write prompts. The problem is something more interesting. We're using incredibly powerful AI systems to answer questions that are often too vague to be useful. Think about how developers commonly interact with AI: "Write this function." "Fix this bug." "Optimize this code." "Explain this error." "Make this application better." These instructions aren't necessarily wrong. But they leave almost everything important to interpretation. What constraints should the AI consider? What would a successful result look like? What assumptions is it making? How should we verify its suggestions?

articles.excerpt: To send email through a queue in Laravel 13, set QUEUE_CONNECTION to a real driver such as database or redis, create a mailable, send it with Mail::to($user)->queue(new WelcomeMail($user)), and run ph…
articles.body: To send email through a queue in Laravel 13, set QUEUE_CONNECTION to a real driver such as database or redis , create a mailable, send it with Mail::to($user)->queue(new WelcomeMail($user)) , and run php artisan queue:work . The web request returns immediately while the worker delivers the message. What do you need before you start? Laravel 13 on PHP 8.3 or newer Working mail settings in .env (a local tool such as Mailpit or Mailtrap is fine) A queue backend. The database driver needs no extra software How do you configure the queue? # .env QUEUE_CONNECTION = database MAIL_MAILER = smtp MAIL_HOST = 127.0 . 0.1 MAIL_PORT = 1025 The database driver stores jobs in a jobs table. New Laravel apps ship with the migration, so migrating is enough.

articles.body: Earlier this year, OnePlus unceremoniously shut down operations in the US and Europe . While this decision means the brand no longer sells its hardware in these markets, it resulted in another change for current users: OxygenOS is on the way out . Future OnePlus software updates will be based on ColorOS, the skin that pilots OPPO devices. Given that the two brands belong to the same parent company, it seemed only a matter of time. The two skins share many commonalities, but as my colleague Dhruv experienced recently running ColorOS 17 on his OnePlus 15 , they couldn’t look or feel more different.

articles.title: 'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight
articles.excerpt: SpaceX has inked a familiar phrase on the Starship rocket that will fly a historic mission today (Nov. 13) — "Don't panic." And the company has invoked those words before.
articles.body: SpaceX has a message for itself, and for the spacecraft set to make history today (Nov. 13): Don't panic. The company's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms. On Thursday (Nov. 12), SpaceX rolled the Flight 15 upper stage, a vehicle known as Ship 42, out to the launch pad at its Starbase site in South Texas to prep. The company shared photos of the move on X , and in two of those shots we can see some intriguing words inked on the spacecraft: "Don't panic." Another look at Ship 42 at the pad on Nov. 12.

articles.title: Netflix's Disappointing New Western Thriller Wastes Its Brilliant Concept
articles.excerpt: Netflix’s Heartland is a western, a noir, and a musical starring Jessica Chastain. It’s also surprisingly predictable.
articles.body: Written and directed by Shana Feste, the Netflix-original film feels as if the director of Country Strong watched a couple of episodes of Yellowstone and decided to take a stab at a western-noir, centering her story on a jaded country star. The result is a missing-person mystery with three musical numbers woven into it. Heartland might be the first western-noir-musical ever made, and I wish Feste took advantage of how weird that is. Instead, it’s pure straight-to-Netflix fodder.

articles.title: Meta brings Pixel-like Call for Me features to Muse for $20/month
articles.excerpt: Muse can now handle business calls, just like Google's Pixel.
articles.body: TL;DR Meta’s Muse can now make phone calls to US businesses for paid subscribers, starting at $20/month. The feature works similarly to Google’s Pixel Call for Me, handling tasks such as restaurant reservations and customer service inquiries. Grok Bot can already call consenting individuals, while Google is exploring similar capabilities for Gemini. Google’s Gemini has already learned to sit through hold music, navigate phone menus, and speak to businesses on your behalf. The feature even expanded to Pixel 10 phones this week. Now, Meta wants its own AI assistant to take those unwanted calls off your hands. Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, announced on X that Muse can now make outgoing calls for paid subscribers in the US.

articles.title: 26 Years Later, Charles Schulz' Final Comic Strip Is Still an All-Time Peanuts Classic
articles.excerpt: 26 Years Later, Charles Schulz' Final Comic Strip Is Still an All-Time Peanuts Classic
articles.body: While that was the first official Peanuts comic, a similar version by Charles Schulz predated Peanuts and ran in Minnesota’s St. Paul Pioneer Press. It was called Li’l Folks and also starred cute little children, although it did not have a regular cast like Peanuts would. Li’l Folks ran from 1947 until 1950, when Schulz quit after his editor refused to give him a raise from the $10 per comic he was making. After that, Schulz brought Li’l Folks to United Feature Syndicate. The national cartoon syndicator liked the comic, but needed to change its name because of a 1930s comic strip called Little Folks .

articles.title: Google Sheets now lets others explore your data without accessing your spreadsheet
articles.excerpt: Let your data do the talking, without revealing everything else.
articles.body: TL;DR Google Sheets now lets users publish Gemini-powered Canvas dashboards, calendars, and task boards through shareable links. People can interact with a published Canvas without accessing or editing the original spreadsheet. Users can control who sees the Canvas and choose whether it updates automatically when spreadsheet data changes. Google Sheets is great for organizing information, but sharing it with others isn’t always convenient. Say you’re managing a project with multiple deadlines and tasks. You might have everything organized in a spreadsheet, but no one wants to scroll through dozens of rows just to see what’s happening next. Google already has a feature called Canvas that uses Gemini to turn spreadsheet data into interactive dashboards, calendars, and task boards.

articles.body: TL;DR Google Health version 5.12.2 is rolling out with a fix for missing vitals and other health metrics. Google has confirmed that the issue affected a small number of iOS users. No health data was lost, and updating the app should restore the missing readings. It’s been a frustrating stretch for Fitbit owners using iPhones. Between syncing and pairing problems affecting the Fitbit Air and disappearing health metrics in Google Health , keeping tabs on their fitness hasn’t exactly been smooth sailing. At least one of those headaches now has an official fix. Google has confirmed to Android Authority that it’s rolling out Google Health version 5.12.2 to resolve the missing vitals issue that emerged following the release of version 5.12 last week.

Microsoft 365 users reported a massive outage yesterday (November 12), affecting Outlook , Teams, Copilot 365 and more. articles.body: SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live. Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX plans to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before. You can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan. articles.title: 'Man of Tomorrow': Release date, plot, cast & everything we know about the 'Superman' sequel
articles.excerpt: James Gunn's new DC universe might be done, but the follow-up to 2025's Superman is still on the way.
articles.body: It feels like yesterday when we were discussing Superman , the first big-screen entry in James Gunn's rebooted DCU. Now Gunn is out , and Skydance (the company formed by the merger of Warner and Paramount) is already dismantling his grand plans for the DCU. That means that Man of Tomorrow, which arrives next summer, will be the final entry in Gunn's ambitious, and occasionally divisive, DC experiment. The DCU's first chapter — officially titled 'Gods and Monsters' — gave us Supergirl and Clayface (as well as TV shows like Peacemaker S2 and Lanterns ) in the run-up to Clark Kent and Lex Luthor 's return.

articles.title: This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star
articles.excerpt: A hidden black hole or neutron star companion to an unstable massive star is causing the system to erupt in light that mimics a supernova explosion.
articles.body: A cosmic imposter that has faked being a supernova 27 times and counting is actually a hot, luminous, and decidedly unstable star that is being fed on by a vampiric black hole or neutron star, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has discovered. When a massive star reaches the end of the road and runs out of nuclear fuel to power fusion reactions in its core, the star is destroyed in a supernova explosion. That’s what astronomers thought they had found on 11 January 2012, when they observed what appeared to be a supernova on the outskirts of the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, which is about 25 million light-years away in the constellation Coma Berenices. Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days.
